CHIEF COMPLAINT
Anxiety follow-up and routine preventive care.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports that anxiety has improved since starting Buspar, prescribed by Dr. Brown. She notes that in November and December, she experienced severe anxiety that started during the day at work. She was uncertain of the etiology but noted that Dr. Ward had started her on Singulair and warned that it can cause anxiety. She observed that the week before her period, her anxiety would spike significantly, and then it progressed to anxiety spiking at random times seemingly without reason. She attributes some of the stress to work, including leading the process of delivering COVID results to patients and opening evaluation centers and COVID clinics during the pandemic. She also noted guilt about not being on the front lines in the ICU. She reports that her symptoms have now settled. She also notes that she stopped taking Camila birth control due to increased hunger at a new high level, and she is now feeling better. She reports weight loss over the past six months. Regarding breast concerns, she notes that lumps that had been present are now smaller but still present. She reports pain in her left breast where she previously had clogs and soreness during breastfeeding. She remains concerned given her age (almost 40) and family history of breast cancer in her mother at age 45.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies weight loss currently, though reports weight loss over past six months. She reports continued itching or discomfort in the vulvovaginal area, managed with cream use once weekly, which helps. She denies other issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Abnormal Pap smear around 2009, requiring follow-up every six months for a period, which then normalized. Breast lumps and cysts. Hormonal issues related to menstrual regulation. History of breastfeeding with clogged ducts and soreness.

MEDICATIONS
Buspar (started by Dr. Brown for anxiety). Progesterone (for regulating periods). Vulvovaginal cream (used once weekly).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at approximately age 45. Husband and daughter unvaccinated against COVID with concerns about long-term effects.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in healthcare setting, involved in COVID testing and clinic operations. Son has received first COVID vaccine dose. Patient has received COVID vaccine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Patient able to take deep breaths without difficulty.
Neck: Small bumps palpated; patient notes they are smaller than previously.
Breast: Left breast noted to be somewhat denser. Tenderness elicited on left breast. Lumps palpated bilaterally; patient reports they are smaller than before but still present.
Pelvic: Appears normal.

RESULTS
Pap smear from 2019 was negative/negative. Prior abnormal Pap in 2009.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Well-controlled on Buspar. Continue current management.
2. Breast concerns: Benign breast issues (cysts, lumps, fibroadenomas) noted. Will continue monitoring. Patient is to follow up with breast specialist; referral to be sent. Breast specialist will contact patient within next couple of business days to schedule appointment. Specialist may perform ultrasound and has experience with procedures if needed.
3. Pap smear: Repeat Pap smear to be performed due to time since last negative result in 2019 and increased risk of abnormalities related to stress and immunocompromising factors during pandemic period.
4. Vulvovaginal itching/discomfort: Continue vulvovaginal cream once weekly. Prescription to be refilled.
